soundness_flags.label: def:two-cohort-estimator; def:standard-error-and-gate; def:hybrid-interval; thm:uniform-gated-inference
soundness_flags.one_line: O_T records only terminally revealed outcomes linked to assignments, not revelation timestamps or delays, so it cannot determine D<=m_T versus m_T<D<=h_T and hence X, R, the estimator, and the asserted O_T-measurability are undefined from the stated observed experiment.

soundness_flags.label: def:followup-tail-radius; prop:wald-followup-frontier; prop:clinical-followup-rule
soundness_flags.one_line: Changing B_{T,Delta} does not redefine the fixed-quota estimator or its old-cohort age h_T, so the proposed post-recruitment follow-up cannot affect I_T^W as currently constructed.

soundness_flags.label: ass:rare-arm-envelope
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Shi--Wang--Wu condition is a one-sided lower forced-exploration bound, whereas this load-bearing assumption imposes a two-sided comparable-to-t^{-alpha} allocation rate that determines the claimed sampling frontier.

soundness_flags.label: ass:eventual-revelation and ass:polynomial-delay-envelope
soundness_flags.one_line: The polynomial envelope with beta>0 implies P(D=+infinity)=lim_u P(D>u)=0, so eventual revelation is redundant.

soundness_flags.label: ass:rare-arm-envelope and ass:control-floor
soundness_flags.one_line: For allowed constants c+epsilon>1, the two-arm simplex makes pi_t(1)>=c and pi_t(0)>=epsilon jointly impossible at t=1; impose c+epsilon<=1 or restrict the parameter domain.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary 4.4 assumes only pi_t(a)>=C t^{-alpha}, together with a delay-tail condition; it does not state the proposal's upper bound pi_t(1)<=C t^{-alpha}.
The paper studies reward-dependent delays and regret; Theorem 6 constructs delayed indistinguishable reward instances for a regret lower bound.
Assumption 1 imposes an arm-uniform polynomial delay-tail bound, while the model generates reward and delay independently.
The paper studies strongly reward-dependent delays and proves regret guarantees and lower bounds, not confidence-interval coverage for an eventual arm contrast.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear regression functionals under normal errors with known variance.
The paper gives adaptively weighted AIPW-style inference with asymptotically normal statistics for adaptive experiments.
The CADR paper identifies construction of adaptive consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimators as its central technical challenge and proves contextual adaptive inference.

The publisher confirms the cited paper and its delayed-outcome CARA semiparametric-efficiency framing; the full text was inaccessible, so the proposal's more specific conditional-independence and overlap comparison remains for source verification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add each outcome's calendar revelation timestamp to O_T, define the terminal data-derived X and R indicators from it, and explicitly rebuild the two-cohort estimator after follow-up Delta_T.

Retag the two-sided rare-arm envelope as a novel design regime with a practical justification, or weaken the main theorem to the published one-sided exploration condition and rederive its rate; also impose c+epsilon<=1.

State a direct restriction theorem showing precisely how the proposed frontier reduces to the Shi--Wang--Wu regime under outcome-delay independence and differs from the Tang/Lancewicki reward-dependent regret regimes.

recommended_next_step: Revise the observed-data definition, the follow-up estimator, and the nonstandard allocation regime before advancing this otherwise field-grade novelty kernel to Stage 0.
